ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders holding not less than 25% of shares or voting rights, all directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the consolidated European Union financial sanctions list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions list, the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the Luxembourg domestic financial and counter-terrorism blacklists; enhanced due diligence for Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) as defined by FATF Recommendation 12 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 14 December 2004; continuous adverse media monitoring and negative news checks required under CSSF circulars.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) electronic portal, in coordination with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu and the notary's e-filing access
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Latin script and are required to use one of the three administrative languages of Luxembourg (French, German, or Luxembourgish) for the mandatory suffix. Depending on the chosen availability check, names in other languages must be exact transliterations into Latin script. The name must be clearly distinguishable from existing registered names and must not create confusion with protected trademarks. The full legal name of an SARL must contain the words 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A name reservation is renewable for consecutive 30-day periods until incorporation, provided the renewal fee is paid and the RCS officer approves the extension. If the Luxembourg Business Registers refuses the proposed name on the grounds of distinctiveness, public order, or prohibited token usage, the applicant may within 90 days of written refusal file a formal administrative appeal through the Luxembourg notary with the Ministry of Justice (Ministère de la Justice). If the Ministry grants a negative decision or fails to respond, the applicant may initiate judicial review proceedings before the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif). Upon final rejection, the applicant must submit an alternative name and pay the applicable reservation fee again.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only through an approved domiciliation agent registered under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies. The SARL must maintain a full street address in Luxembourg within the territorial jurisdiction; remote e-commerce operations are compatible with domiciliation provided the company retains real commercial substance, namely material operational records, human presence where applicable, and VAT accounting substance. Domiciliation without economic substance will contravene Luxembourg tax abuse rules and the law of 19 December 2012 on the commercial register.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated 12-18% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first 24 months from incorporation, based on the low-risk standard e-commerce profile, mandatory VAT registration thresholds, import customs supervision of portable batteries and solar panels, and potential tax substance verification actions by the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Articles 180-1 to 190-1 (Société à Responsabilité Limitée) and associated RCS/notarial provisions
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association (Statuts) filed with the RCS
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: EUR 12,000 minimum share capital, fully subscribed and paid in cash. Subscription monies must be placed on a blocked account with a Luxembourg credit institution until the RCS registration certificate is issued, after which the account is released to the company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 100 shares of EUR 120 each, is fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the bank blocked-account certificate. RESOLVED that the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg. RESOLVED that [Manager] is appointed manager with full authority to manage, bind and represent the company, to open bank accounts, and to file all required documents with the RCS, tax and social security authorities. RESOLVED that [Bank] is designated as principal bank.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name availability search and reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) online portal at www.lbr.lu - RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the RCS database for identical or confusingly similar corporate names. If available, submit an online name-reservation request through the LBR e-platform, attaching the proposed articles and shareholder identification. Once approved, preserve the reservation reference for the notary. The notary will recheck the name immediately before execution.
required_dossiers: Completed name-search and reservation form
Identification documents of all shareholders
Statement of corporate purpose and proposed articles draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a different name or appeal to the RCS registry office with a revised request. If a similarity conflict arises, obtain a written waiver from the prior user or amend the corporate name sufficiently before notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and execute notarial Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ordre des Notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Luxembourg notary to prepare the final statuts in French, German, or Luxembourgish. The shareholders appear physically before the notary or execute by authenticated power of attorney. The notary verifies identity, capacity, name reservation, and subscription of capital, then authenticates the Articles of Association and prepares the RCS filing extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Association (statuts)
Power of attorney for each non-appearing shareholder
Copy of the name reservation reference
Passports or identification documents of shareholders and managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires corrections, execute an amendatory addendum or a revised deed and pay the additional notarial fee. If any supporting document is missing, submit it within the notary's deadline and re-authenticate the instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked share capital account and deposit minimum capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution authorised by the CSSF
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account in the name of the SARL en formation at a Luxembourg bank. Transfer the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 from the shareholders' accounts. Instruct the bank to block funds until presentation of the RCS registration certificate. Obtain the bank's blocked-account statement (attestation de blocage) for inclusion in the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Account opening application and bank KYC forms
Final or draft Articles of Association
Identification and source-of-funds documentation for shareholders and managers
Declaration of beneficial ownership details for bank due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests further KYC or source-of-wealth details, provide prompt supplemental evidence. If the transfer fails or is delayed by SWIFT, resend with the corporate reference and obtain a fresh blocked-account certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete incorporation dossier through the LBR e-filing module. Include the notarial engrossment, blocked-account certificate, statement of registered office address, signed acceptance of manager appointment, and identification of managers. Pay the applicable RCS registration fee. Upon registration, the RCS issues the company's registration extract and Luxembourg registration number.
required_dossiers: Authenticated notarial deed of incorporation
Bank blocked-account certificate
Manager appointment acceptance and identification
Proof of registered office address or domiciliation agreement
Statement of corporate purpose and proposed activity codes
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the filing, respond through the LBR portal within the prescribed period with corrections or supplementary documents. If the dossier is incomplete, resubmit the amended filing and pay any additional fee. If the blocked-account certificate has expired, obtain a reissued certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and mandatory post-registration filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RESA and Guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the LBR publishes the legal incorporation notice in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA). Register the company for VAT through Guichet.lu, register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), file the ultimate beneficial owner declaration with the LBR, and, if employees will be engaged, declare the activity to the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM).
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate or extract
Notarized Articles of Association
VAT and social security application forms
Ultimate beneficial owner declaration
Statement of actual business start date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If RESA publication is delayed, contact the LBR helpdesk. If VAT, CCSS, or beneficial owner filings are rejected, correct the electronic form and resubmit immediately. If a requested document is missing, obtain a certified copy and file it with the registry.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - no industrial operator licence is required for direct online retail of portable solar power equipment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from EIA and environmental permitting where the activity is limited to online retail and small-scale warehousing. However, the company may need to register as a battery producer under Luxembourg waste-battery law if it places portable battery generators on the market.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No wastewater or VOC permit thresholds apply to the retail activity. Compliance with EU Battery Regulation 2023/1542 and national transposition is required; waste batteries must be returned through an approved take-back scheme, and storage or transport of lithium-ion batteries must observe ADR Class 9 rules when quantities exceed exempt thresholds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: If the SARL maintains a warehouse or physical storage area for panels and batteries, municipal fire safety inspection and a structural load certificate for racking are required. Occupational safety clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines applies only when employees are engaged; office-only e-commerce operations are not subject to industrial fire certification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des Contributions Directes, ACD) for direct income/corporate taxes — https://impotsdirects.public.lu; VAT and registration taxes: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — https://pfi.public.lu (VAT e-filing, OSS/IOSS portal); central business formalities portal: https://guichet.lu; Companies Register: Luxembourg Business Registers, https://www.lbr.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the SARL before a Luxembourg notary, deposit minimum capital (EUR 12,000 for a standard SARL), and file the articles with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS) to obtain the RCS registration number. Step 2: ACD automatically allocates the 11-digit direct-tax matricule/TIN upon registration; confirm the matricule via the guichet.lu eSpace. Step 3: Apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number in the format 'LU' + 8 digits (the same number can be used for OSS/IOSS if the entity elects distance-sales rules); VAT registration is mandatory before the first taxable supply in Luxembourg and can be completed electronically within days. Foreign shareholders are permitted without local residency; the SARL must appoint a resident manager (gérant) satisfying substance requirements.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — the SARL is a fully opaque Luxembourg tax-resident corporation taxed on worldwide profits; no domestic pass-through treatment applies. Qualifying dividends and capital gains may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption; no pure territorial regime and no special tax-exempt zone applies to the entity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections and mechanisms: (1) fiscal integration (tax consolidation) for a 95%-owned group of Luxembourg subsidiaries; (2) application for a VAT group (unité TVA) with AEDT approval; (3) OSS/IOSS registration so that intra-EU distance sales and certain imports are declared centrally instead of through destination-country VAT registrations; (4) binding tax rulings and advance pricing agreements with ACD; (5) election to apply the Luxembourg participation exemption on substantiated shareholdings; (6) mandatory ATAD/hybrid mismatch analysis where a foreign parent's check-the-box or similar classification could recharacterize the SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Luxembourg VAT Code (Loi du 12 février 1979 sur la TVA, as amended), fully aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/CE.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For a Luxembourg-established SARL: mandatory VAT registration from the first euro of taxable turnover (no general registration threshold). A small-business exemption ('franchise en base') is available up to EUR 35,000 annual turnover, but it does not apply to cross-border distance sales or OSS-managed supplies. For intra-EU distance sales of goods: EUR 10,000 annual EU-wide threshold applies; above that threshold, VAT is due in the destination EU Member State. Non-established foreign sellers must register as soon as they make their first taxable supply in Luxembourg unless OSS/IOSS or a marketplace deemed-supplier rule applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg currently has no real-time fiscal clearance system, no mandatory e-invoicing, and no digital stamping or API clearance mandate. E-invoicing is permitted and Peppol BIS, UBL, Factur-X and EN 16931 formats are accepted; paper invoices remain lawful for B2B and B2C transactions. A mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime is expected under the EU 'VAT in the Digital Age' (ViDA) package, with Luxembourg transposition planned on the 2030/2035 horizon; until then, taxpayers must retain full invoice archives for 10 years and file periodic VAT returns, recapitulative statements (EC Sales Lists) and OSS returns through the AEDT eSpace portal.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with credit) applies to: (a) exports of portable battery generators and solar panels to non-EU destinations under Art. 41 Loi TVA, provided the goods are physically dispatched outside the EU customs territory within 3 months of the supply and conclusive customs/transport evidence is retained; (b) intra-Community supplies to EU VAT-registered businesses under Art. 43 Loi TVA, requiring the buyer's valid EU VAT ID, physical movement to another Member State, and EC Sales List reporting; (c) certain export-related services such as freight and forwarding directly linked to the exported goods. Supplies to private EU consumers are not zero-rated: cross-border distance sales exceeding the EUR 10,000 annual EU-wide threshold are taxable in the consumer's destination Member State and reportable through OSS. Because Stripe and Affirm BNPL act as payment intermediaries and not online marketplaces, the deemed-supplier regime does not displace the SARL's VAT liability on such sales.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (electronic DAU filed via Luxembourg Customs PLDA or the export declaration of the Member State of export)
Commercial invoice, order confirmation and packing list evidencing the buyer, goods and sales terms
Bill of Lading / CMR waybill / air waybill or equivalent carrier-issued proof of dispatch from EU to non-EU destination
Bank transfer, Stripe settlement record or other payment-rail evidence of inward remittance
For intra-Community zero-rating: purchaser's valid VAT identification number and the periodic EC Sales List / VIES record
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are jointly audited by AEDT (VAT) and customs authorities. Failure to evidence physical export within the 3-month dispatch period, or failure to retain supporting documents for the statutory 10-year retention period, triggers retrospective VAT reassessment at 17% plus monthly arrears interest of 0.8% and administrative fines from EUR 750 to EUR 12,500 per infringement under Art. 65 Loi TVA. Intentional or fraudulent zero-rating, including sham exports, participation in missing-trader fraud chains and false EC Sales Lists, is criminally sanctionable with fines up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment of responsible managers for up to 5 years; unduly paid refunds are clawed back with additional late-payment penalties up to 10% of the assessed VAT.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; day-to-day supervision of credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); monetary and foreign-exchange competence is delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB) and the European Union institutions under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full currency convertibility with no exchange-control approval requirements for current-account or capital-account operations. The euro is fully convertible; capital injections, shareholder loans, trade payments, intercompany disbursements and profit repatriation require no central bank permit and are unrestricted under Article 63 TFEU and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. The only operational friction for profit remittance is the domestic 15% dividend withholding tax, reducible to 0% for qualifying EU/EEA corporate shareholders under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, plus standard CRS/FATCA documentation duties. All balances may be held or converted in any currency through CSSF-licensed credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export-proceeds surrender regime, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no compulsory repatriation timeline exist in Luxembourg. Export receipts derived by the SARL from distance sales of portable solar power equipment may be retained indefinitely in EUR or foreign currency in any CSSF-licensed bank account. The only compliance duties are indirect BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting performed by the bank for individual transactions at or above EUR 12,500, together with standard EU VAT distance-selling and One-Stop-Shop (OSS) declarations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) for share capital
Operational corporate account (EUR/USD) with daily treasury sweeping

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (compte bloqué) for share capital

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational corporate account (SEPA and SWIFT) linked to e-commerce payment gateways
Operational treasury account (EUR/USD/CNY) with correspondent clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: HIGH as a payment-acquiring rail, LOW as a primary treasury account. EU/EEA-authorized digital EMIs operating in Luxembourg under PSD2/EMD2 passporting (Stripe, PayPal and Wise Europe based in Ireland/Belgium) may lawfully process online card flows and Affirm BNPL settlements, but balances held with these non-bank institutions are not safeguarded under the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDL). Offshore non-EEA EMIs have no legal standing to provide core banking or FX clearing services to a Luxembourg SARL and cannot be used for the capital escrow or for shareholder distributions. Consequently, the SARL should maintain Tier-1 bank accounts at BIL/BCEE as the sole treasury ledger and automate same-day sweeping from the EMI collection balances.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In substance, a physical KYC interview is mandatory at all Tier-1 Luxembourg banks: at least one director or UBO of the SARL (or a formally appointed Luxembourg-resident authorised signatory) must attend an in-person onboarding meeting, normally at the commercial banking desk, before the capital escrow account can be activated. Remote onboarding via eIDAS-compliant video identification is legally available under CSSF AML guidance, yet BIL, BCEE and BNP Paribas routinely require a physical meeting for newly incorporated SARLs with non-resident shareholders. Expected onboarding timeline: 3–5 weeks for KYC, plus a further 1–2 weeks for operational account activation after RCS registration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with no employees, no operational history and no audited financial statements, creating shell-like substance concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised articles of incorporation (statuts), RCS registration extract, written lease for a registered Luxembourg office, Luxembourg social security registration (CCSS), CVs of managers and shareholders, VAT registration certificate, detailed e-commerce business plan, supplier contracts, warehouse/logistics agreements and the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial-owner opacity in the cross-border shareholding chain, including nominee shareholders or non-EU corporate parents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RBE extract naming every natural-person UBO with direct or indirect ownership above 25%, notarial UBO declaration, corporate shareholder resolutions, board minutes appointing signatories, powers of attorney, source-of-funds bank statements for each contributor and sworn English/French/German translations of all constitutive documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce payment profile exhibiting high volumes of small personal transfers, rapid refund velocity and large monthly payouts from Stripe/Affirm BNPL aggregators.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Stripe and BNPL monthly settlement reports, ERP order-to-invoice-to-shipment logs, courier and customs documentation (CN22/CN23), refund policy disclosures, SSL/3DS transaction verification records, customer correspondence samples and a written explanation of the commercial model supporting each recurring settlement batch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed persons (PEP) screening alerts triggered by distant customers or by suppliers of solar panels and battery generators in third countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated sanctions/PEP screening policy and audit trail, geo-blocking configuration restricting sales from sanctioned jurisdictions, product classification memo confirming solar portable power equipment is a non-dual-use consumer good outside EU Annex I controls, supplier KYC questionnaires and export invoices referencing the ISIC 4791 e-commerce profile.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Share capital must be wired in EUR to the capital escrow account (compte bloqué) opened with BIL or BCEE prior to the RCS registration filing; EU shareholders may use SEPA Credit Transfer/SEPA Instant while non-EU shareholders should use SWIFT MT103. The required remittance reference is 'Share capital contribution to LU SARL - RCS Luxembourg B###### - Notary [name]', with the ISO 20022 purpose code 'INVE' (investment); the receiving bank automatically maps the transaction to the BCL balance-of-payments code for direct investment equity capital. Verification bundle: notarised draft statuts, RBE UBO filing, contributor bank statements evidencing legitimate funds, corporate resolutions and powers of attorney for corporate shareholders, passports of subscribing individuals and a notary instruction letter confirming the minimum paid-up capital of at least EUR 12,000 is held in cleared funds.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements in EUR are cleared via SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for EU component suppliers; USD payments to Chinese or US manufacturers of portable solar panels and battery generators are executed via SWIFT MT103 with correspondent routing through CHIPS/Fedwire New York; CNY and CNH payments are routed through the bank's RMB clearing desk or via CNH offshore accounts in Hong Kong. For bulk procurement orders above EUR 100,000, irrevocable documentary Letters of Credit (UCP 600) or standby LCs are permissible where the supplier bank is acceptable to BIL/BCEE. Every outbound wire must carry the purchase order number, Incoterms (EXW/FOB/CIF), commercial invoice, packing list and a non-dual-use classification statement; all payments are screened against EU consolidated sanctions lists and CSSF/BCL AML obligations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable EUR/USD and EUR/CNH forward contracts with tenors of 1 to 12 months matched to purchase-order inventory cycles, executed under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement with a CSSF-licensed counterparty
EUR/USD foreign-exchange swaps used solely for temporary liquidity smoothing between EU collection cycles and Asian disbursement cycles
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for matched working-capital financing when USD supplier credit is converted into EUR-denominated debt
Deliverable offshore CNY (CNH) forwards linked to mainland Chinese supply-chain disbursements
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/CNY permitted only through the Luxembourg bank's trade desk, fully collateralised and reported under EMIR as a Non-Financial Counterparty (NFC-)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting approval of statutory annual accounts, allocation of profit or loss, and discharge of managers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate statutory records at the registered office; no public filing required unless reserved matters are voted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each financial year; calendar-year SARL: on or before 30 June of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Accounts cannot be validly filed with the RCS without timely shareholder approval; managers lose the benefit of discharge and may face civil liability for irregular distributions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual accounts, including balance sheet, profit-and-loss account and notes, and auditor's report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; calendar-year SARL: approval by 30 June and RCS deposit by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court-ordered filing under daily coercive penalties (astreinte); criminal fines for continued non-filing; repeated default can trigger judicial strike-off or dissolution of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return for corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes – ACD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due within six months after tax year-end; administrative extension for calendar-year e-filing taxpayers typically permits filing by 31 December of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Ex officio assessment; late-payment interest at 0.8% per month; surcharges up to 10% of the assessed tax; criminal penalties for non-filing after formal summons

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial ownership register (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the eJustice portal; RBE registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January based on data held on 1 January; any share transfer or control change requires a further RBE update within one month after the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines and, for intentional omissions, imprisonment sanctions under the Law of 13 January 2019; continued breach may support public disclosure of the default and director disqualification
